summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted after an outside hospital reported a positive blood culture with gram-positive cocci. Repeat cultures were negative, and the initial result was deemed a contaminant. She presented with worsening lower extremity edema due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, following a self-reduction of her diuretic regimen. She was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned back to Bumex 4 mg twice daily. Her cough, attributed to viral bronchitis, improved with continued azithromycin and a prednisone taper. Phenytoin levels were subtherapeutic, prompting a dose increase to 900 mg daily after a brief seizure-like episode. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved fluid status, and plans for outpatient lab monitoring of phenytoin, INR, and electrolytes.
